q: Which choice most logically completes the text?

items.p: Bees visit flowers to collect nectar and pollen. Researchers placed identical feeders filled with sugar water in a garden, painting some blue and some white. Over a week, bees visited the blue feeders far more often than the white ones. This result suggests that the bees ______
c: may be more attracted to blue than to white.
cannot see the color white.
prefer sugar water to nectar.
visit only blue flowers in the wild.
w: Bees did visit white feeders, just less often.
Sugar water and nectar were never compared.
The study involved feeders, not wild flowers, and says nothing about "only."
items.e: The feeders differed only in color, so the difference in visits points to a preference for blue.

items.p: A bakery noticed that its bread sold out by noon on days when it opened at 6 a.m., but bread was often left over on days when it opened at 8 a.m. Because many customers buy bread on their way to work, the owner concluded that ______
c: opening earlier lets the bakery reach more of its morning customers.
customers prefer bread baked in the afternoon.
the bakery should close at noon every day.
customers never buy bread on weekends.
w: Afternoon baking is never discussed.
Selling out by noon doesn't mean the bakery should close then.
Weekends are never mentioned.
items.e: If customers buy bread on the way to work, opening before they commute captures those sales.

items.p: Glaciers form when snow builds up over many years and is compressed into ice. In a mountain range where yearly snowfall has declined for decades while summer temperatures have risen, scientists would most likely expect the glaciers to ______
c: shrink over time.
grow larger each year.
stay exactly the same size.
form more quickly than before.
w: Less snow and more melting both work against growth.
Both trends change the ice.
Less snowfall means less new ice.
items.e: Less snow adds less ice and warmer summers melt more, so the glaciers should shrink.

items.p: In a study, students who took handwritten notes during a lecture later remembered more of it than students who typed notes, even though the typists recorded more words. The researchers suggested that because handwriting is slower, students must decide what to write, which requires them to ______
c: think about and summarize the material as they listen.
copy the lecture word for word.
ignore most of the lecture.
type faster than they can write.
w: Slow handwriting makes word-for-word copying impossible.
They remembered more, so they did not ignore it.
This doesn't follow from handwriting being slow.
items.e: Choosing what to write means processing and condensing ideas, which may explain the better memory.

items.p: A city added a lane for buses only on its busiest street. Before the lane opened, buses on that route took an average of 40 minutes; afterward, the same trip took 28 minutes, while traffic on nearby streets did not change. These results suggest that the bus lane ______
c: shortened bus travel times on that route.
slowed traffic on nearby streets.
made the buses slower.
had no effect on bus travel.
w: Traffic on nearby streets did not change.
Travel time fell from 40 to 28 minutes.
Travel times clearly changed.
items.e: Trips got 12 minutes shorter with no change elsewhere, which points to the bus lane.

items.p: The seeds of many plants can remain dormant in soil for years, sprouting only when conditions become favorable. After a fire cleared the tall trees shading a hillside, botanists found many seedlings of a species that had not been seen there for decades. The botanists concluded that seeds of the species had most likely ______
c: been lying dormant in the soil until sunlight reached it.
been created by the heat of the fire.
never been present on the hillside before.
grown only in deep shade.
w: Fire doesn't create seeds.
The species had grown there before, decades earlier.
The seedlings appeared only after the shade was removed.
items.e: Dormant seeds can wait for favorable conditions, and removing the shade provided them.

items.p: Two identical apartment buildings were built side by side, one painted white and the other dark gray. During a summer heat wave, residents of the gray building used their air conditioners much more often than residents of the white building. A likely explanation is that the gray building ______
c: absorbed more heat from the sun than the white building did.
had fewer residents than the white building.
stayed cooler than the white building.
had no air conditioners.
w: The buildings are identical except for color.
More air-conditioner use suggests it was hotter.
Its residents used air conditioners.
items.e: The buildings differ only in color, and dark surfaces absorb more sunlight, so the gray building likely got hotter.

items.p: Linguists have observed that words for everyday objects tend to be short, while words for rare things tend to be longer. One explanation is that speakers shorten words they use often to save effort. If this explanation is correct, a newly invented device that becomes common in daily life would most likely ______
c: come to be called by a shorter name over time.
keep its original long name permanently.
be named after its inventor.
be described using several separate words.
w: The explanation predicts that frequent words get shorter.
The explanation says nothing about inventors.
This would make the name longer, not shorter.
items.e: If frequent use leads speakers to shorten words, a device that becomes common should get a shorter name.

items.p: Farmers who planted strips of wildflowers along the edges of their fields found fewer crop pests than farmers who did not. The wildflowers support insects that prey on pests, and these predators depend on flowers for food when pests are scarce. Removing the wildflower strips would therefore most likely ______
c: reduce the number of predatory insects and allow pests to increase.
increase the number of predatory insects.
have no effect on pest numbers.
eliminate crop pests entirely.
w: The predators depend on the flowers.
The flowers support the predators that control pests.
Fewer predators would mean more pests, not none.
items.e: Without flowers, predators lose a food source. Fewer predators means more pests.

items.p: The ancient city of Toreth was known for its pottery. Archaeologists have found Toreth-style pots at sites hundreds of miles away, and chemical tests show that the clay in those pots matches deposits found only near Toreth itself. This evidence suggests that the pots ______
c: were made in Toreth and carried to the distant sites.
were made at the distant sites by potters copying Toreth's style.
were never used for trade.
were made from clay found near the distant sites.
w: The clay comes only from near Toreth.
Carrying pots hundreds of miles points to trade.
The tests show the clay came from near Toreth.
items.e: Clay found only near Toreth means the pots were made there, then moved.

items.p: Most owls hunt at night, but one grassland owl species often hunts during the day. Researchers found that in regions where this owl hunts by day, its main prey, a species of vole, is also most active during daylight. The researchers concluded that the owl's hunting schedule is likely shaped by ______
c: when its prey is most active.
the brightness of the moon.
competition with other owls at night.
the temperature of the grasslands.
w: The finding concerns daytime prey activity, not moonlight.
Competition was not studied.
Temperature was not studied.
items.e: The owl hunts by day where its prey is active by day, which suggests the prey drives its schedule.

items.p: A publisher released one novel with two different covers: one with a photograph of a city, the other with an abstract painting. In bookstores that displayed both, the photograph version sold twice as many copies. Online, where buyers mostly saw small thumbnail images, the two versions sold equally well. These results suggest that the photograph cover's advantage ______
c: depended on buyers seeing the cover at full size.
came from a lower price.
existed only for online buyers.
came from the novel's content.
w: Price is never mentioned.
Online, the versions sold equally.
Both versions had the same content.
items.e: The advantage appeared in stores, where covers are seen full size, and vanished online, where they're tiny.

items.p: Spiders of one species weave a thick zigzag band of silk into the center of their webs. Some scientists proposed that the band warns birds, which might otherwise fly through and destroy the web. In a test, webs with the band were damaged by birds far less often than webs from which the band had been removed. The test therefore supports the idea that the band ______
c: helps protect the web from birds.
attracts birds to the web.
helps the web catch more insects.
serves no purpose.
w: Webs with the band were damaged less, not more.
Insect capture was not tested.
Removing the band changed the damage rate.
items.e: Webs with the band suffered less bird damage, which supports its role as a warning.

items.p: Some coastal towns that rely on tourism see their population triple each summer. In one such town, the water treatment plant was built decades ago to serve only the year-round population. Town officials have warned that during the summer months, the plant may ______
c: struggle to handle the much larger demand.
produce far more water than the town needs.
close because too few people use it.
serve only the tourists.
w: Summer demand rises; the plant was built for fewer people.
Summer brings more users, not fewer.
Nothing suggests it would stop serving residents.
items.e: A plant sized for the year-round population would be strained when the population triples.

items.p: Historians have long debated why a medieval river town declined. Some blame a war that reached the region in 1410. Tax records, however, show that the town's income fell steadily for thirty years before the war began, during the same decades in which the river beside it gradually filled with silt and became too shallow for cargo ships. These records suggest that ______
c: the town's decline likely began before the war and may have been driven by the river's silting.
the war was the only cause of the town's decline.
the town's income rose until the war began.
cargo ships avoided the town because of its high taxes.
w: Income was falling decades before the war.
The records show income falling, not rising.
Taxes are the evidence here, not the cause; silt blocked the ships.
items.e: The decline predates the war and coincides with the river becoming too shallow for trade.

items.p: In experiments, people asked to predict how happy they would be a year after a major life event, such as moving to a new city, usually expected strong and lasting effects. When researchers checked in a year later, most people's happiness had returned close to its earlier level. This pattern suggests that people tend to ______
c: overestimate how long the emotional effects of events will last.
underestimate how much events will affect them.
become permanently happier after moving.
be unable to predict anything about their futures.
w: They predicted strong, lasting effects that did not last.
Happiness returned to earlier levels.
This overgeneralizes; the finding concerns emotional duration.
items.e: People expected lasting effects, but happiness returned to its baseline, so they overestimated how long the effects would last.

items.p: Painter Lucia Ferro mixed her own pigments, and her notebooks list the ingredients of every color she used. When conservators analyzed a painting long credited to Ferro, they found a blue pigment that was not manufactured until twenty years after her death. Unless the painting was later retouched, this finding indicates that ______
c: the painting was probably not painted by Ferro, at least not entirely.
Ferro invented the blue pigment herself.
Ferro's notebooks are inaccurate about every color.
the painting was finished before Ferro's death.
w: The pigment didn't exist until after her death.
One pigment doesn't discredit every notebook entry.
A pigment made after her death means some paint was applied after she died.
items.e: Ferro could not have used a pigment that didn't yet exist, so someone else painted at least part of the work.

items.p: A school district introduced a free breakfast program at half of its schools, chosen at random. After a year, attendance rose at the schools with the program but stayed flat at the others, while test scores rose slightly at both groups of schools. Based on these results, the program most likely ______
c: improved attendance, but its effect on test scores is unclear.
caused test scores to rise.
reduced attendance.
had no measurable effect.
w: Scores rose at schools without the program too.
Attendance rose at the program schools.
Attendance rose only where the program ran.
items.e: Random assignment links the attendance gain to the program. Scores rose everywhere, so the program's effect on scores can't be separated out.
